prose.text: An ordinary hand axe, well used, with a carefully oiled head. With iron head and wooden handle, it served two related households for cutting kindling and trimming repair timber; the handle was replaced while the original head was kept.
Several households once shared a single workshop while their own roofs were repaired. Old household tools are passed to a younger relative when a new household is formed.
A bronze survey weight with a line of small punched dots. Made for checking workshop balances, it is remembered by a few local craftspeople for its careful finish.
A ruined structure retains a fallen roof. Built as a watch post several generations ago, it later changed: the entrance was repaired and later abandoned.
